How do you bring the three-quarter waltz into the digital realm without slipping into historical kitsch? For Johann Strauss’s 200th birthday in 2025, our 360° campaign  (created by [Gruppe am Park](https://www.gruppe-am-park.at/project/johann-strauss-2025-wien-programm) for the City of Vienna translated the 19th-century pop star’s joie de vivre straight into the present.

“The kinetic visual system and striking color palette carry effortlessly across both analog and digital touchpoints, giving the anniversary year a clearly legible, contemporary identity.”
Winner of the German Brand Award 2026 — Jury Statement

Because the very first second decides whether a user merely scrolls or truly feels the rhythm, the initial contact had to act like a curtain-raiser. Right upon landing, an elegant spatial animation sets the emblem and 3D objects into motion. Combined with perspective depth-of-field blurs, this opening sequence pulls visitors straight into the swing of Strauss’s work before they even read a single word.

Instead of merely decorating, interactive gradients capture the ~emotion~ of a Viennese sky from sunrise to purple dusk. They reflect a broad cultural ~spectrum~, from opera and choir to circus, while offering intuitive ~orientation~ across the site, balanced by crisp white accents.
